nodes.label: Qwen-AgentWorld: Language World Models for Agent Training
nodes.author: Yuxin Zuo, Zikai Xiao, Li Sheng, Fei Huang, Jianhong Tu
nodes.rationale: Language world models trained via CPT→SFT→RL pipeline to simulate diverse agent environments across 7 domains, enabling both decoupled Sim RL and unified agent foundation models.

nodes.label: AgentWorldBench: LWM Evaluation Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Benchmark pairing every sample with ground-truth observation from real environments, evaluating LWM across five dimensions: Format, Factuality, Consistency, Realism, Quality.

nodes.label: Sim RL: Simulated Reinforcement Learning
nodes.rationale: Training agents in simulated environments generated by LWM, with controllable simulation instructions to inject targeted perturbations and improve agent robustness.

nodes.label: Controllable Simulation: Environment Adaptation & Fictional-World Construction
nodes.rationale: Two complementary modes: (1) Environment Adaptation injects targeted perturbations via natural-language instructions; (2) Fictional-World Construction generates self-consistent fictional environments for search agents.

nodes.label: LWM RL Warm-up: Agent Foundation Model
nodes.rationale: Single-turn LWM RL on next-state prediction transfers to multi-turn tool-calling agentic tasks across seven benchmarks, demonstrating radical cross-task and domain generalization.

nodes.label: Mental Simulation: Prediction-Driven Action Refinement
nodes.rationale: LWM-trained agents systematically perform mental simulation of environment responses before executing actions, using internalized world model to predict outcomes and refine action plans.

nodes.label: LWM Reasoning Patterns: Deliberative Self-Correction, Information Leakage Prevention, Multi-Step Causal Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Three representative reasoning patterns: (1) Deliberative Self-Correction uses 'Wait!' interrupts to revise predictions; (2) Information Leakage Prevention distinguishes agent knowledge from environment revelation; (3) Multi-Step Causal Reasoning chains across system abstractions.

nodes.label: Micro-Level Fidelity Improvements: URL Realism, Byte Arithmetic, API Schema Consistency
nodes.rationale: RL training improves fidelity at fine granularity: URL identifiers, character-level byte arithmetic, cross-turn API schema consistency maintained across multiple sequential calls.

nodes.label: OpenClaw: Out-of-Distribution Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Open-source real-world AI agent platform with tasks from real user multi-step digital workflows (scheduling, coding, email, browser automation, file management), entirely out-of-distribution for testing generalization.

nodes.label: Three-Stage Training Pipeline: CPT→SFT→RL
nodes.rationale: Progressive training: CPT injects environment knowledge, SFT activates next-state-prediction reasoning, RL sharpens simulation fidelity across seven domains.

nodes.label: Seven Agent Interaction Domains
nodes.rationale: Terminal, MCP Tool Use, Search, Software Engineering, Android, Web, OS—covering text-based and GUI-based agent environments.

nodes.label: World-Model–Actor Unification Architecture
nodes.rationale: Same model serves as both agent (action selection) and world model (environment state prediction), aligning with LeCun et al. (2022) vision and World Action Model paradigm.

nodes.label: Claw-Eval & QwenClawBench: Out-of-Domain Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Real-world digital workflow benchmarks entirely absent from LWM training; Sim RL with Qwen-AgentWorld-397B-A17B improves Claw-Eval +4.3 and QwenClawBench +7.1 over base model.

nodes.label: Tool Decathlon & MCPMark: MCP Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Tool Decathlon covers 32 software applications; MCPMark evaluates 127 multi-step tasks; controllable Sim RL improves Tool Decathlon +3.7 and MCPMark +12.3 over uncontrolled baseline.

nodes.label: WideSearch: Fictional-World Search Benchmark
nodes.rationale: 200 manually curated information-seeking tasks; agents trained entirely in fictional environments generalize to real-world search; Qwen3.5-35B-A3B improves F1 Item +16.29, F1 Row +10.49.

nodes.label: Terminal-Bench 2.0: Terminal Agent Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Hard, realistic terminal tasks; LWM RL warm-up improves accuracy +6.30 on single-turn next-state prediction, transferring to multi-turn tool-calling agentic tasks.

nodes.label: SWE-Bench Verified & Pro: Software Engineering Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Real GitHub issues; LWM RL improves SWE-Bench Verified +3.39 and SWE-Bench Pro +5.24 resolve rate, demonstrating transfer from single-turn to multi-turn software engineering tasks.

nodes.label: BFCL v4: Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard
nodes.rationale: Out-of-domain function-calling benchmark; LWM RL improves +9.0 on BFCL v4, confirming transferable agent capabilities rather than domain-specific shortcuts.

nodes.label: Environment Prediction Accuracy Metric
nodes.rationale: Measures fraction of correctly predicted environment responses in thinking traces; LWM RL improves from 69.9% to 78.3% (+8.4%), confirming internal world model becomes more faithful.

nodes.label: Rule-Based Verification: Controllability, Error Handling, Long-Context Consistency
nodes.rationale: Three deterministic verification axes: (1) Controllability (adherence to simulation instructions), (2) Error Handling (faithful error reproduction), (3) Long-Context Consistency (coherent state tracking).

nodes.label: Open-Ended Rubric Evaluation: Five Dimensions
nodes.rationale: Five evaluation dimensions applied across all domains: Format (structural adherence), Factuality (correctness), Consistency (coherence with prior state), Realism (authentic behavior), Quality (completeness/conciseness).

nodes.label: Training Dynamics: Per-Dimension Improvement Rates
nodes.rationale: Format converges within ~90 steps; Consistency requires ~250 steps; Factuality improves most in relative terms (+11.3%) but remains lowest-scoring dimension throughout training.

nodes.label: Qwen Model Variants: 35B-A3B and 397B-A17B
nodes.rationale: Two scales of Qwen-AgentWorld: 35B-A3B (smaller, faster) and 397B-A17B (larger, more capable); both trained via CPT→SFT→RL pipeline across seven domains.

nodes.label: Baseline Comparisons: Qwen3.6-Plus, GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.6
nodes.rationale: Qwen-AgentWorld-397B-A17B competitive with frontier models; rule-based verification shows GPT-5.4 ranks first (72.93 avg), Qwen-AgentWorld-397B-A17B second (67.12), outperforming on GUI domains.

nodes.label: Real RL vs. Sim RL Comparison
nodes.rationale: Controllable Sim RL tracks or exceeds Real RL on WideSearch; Sim RL increases web_extractor calls (2.5→4.0) while Real RL decreases (2.5→1.5), reflecting deliberate information withholding in simulation.

nodes.label: Case Study: Mailman Task - Prediction-Driven Action Refinement
nodes.rationale: Before LWM RL: incorrect prediction of Postfix processing order leads to futile exploration. After LWM RL: correct prediction enables targeted fix to local_recipient_maps, demonstrating mental simulation enabling action refinement.

edges.rationale: Both papers address persistent data management for LLM agents; Qwen-AgentWorld focuses on environment simulation while agent memory focuses on information storage/retrieval, but both are foundational infrastructure for agent execution.
Both address unified agent architectures; world-model–actor unification parallels memory system integration into agent reasoning loops.

hyperedges.label: Agent Infrastructure Ecosystem: World Models + Memory Systems
hyperedges.rationale: Together these concepts form a coherent infrastructure layer for autonomous agents: world models simulate environment dynamics, memory systems persist and retrieve agent state, unified architectures integrate both for improved reasoning and planning.

hyperedges.label: Sim RL Training Paradigm: Simulation + Controllability + Agent Learning
hyperedges.rationale: Sim RL unifies three components: (1) LWM generates simulated environments, (2) controllable simulation injects targeted perturbations, (3) agent RL learns from simulated trajectories, enabling both decoupled and unified training paradigms.
